findings.finding: SURVIVING MUTATION: plan() stops calling task_for and reverts to the pre-fix inline logic, while task_for stays exactly as staged. All three tests pass. Verified by running the mutant: `plan binjava.binstore.VersionTest#x binjava.CoverageGateTest#y` emits ':binstore-spi:test ...' as staged and 'test ...' under the mutation, and every test is green both ways, because all three reach task_for only through the new `task-for` CLI branch (tdd_scan.py:252-258) and nothing asserts over plan's output. Round one's fix moved the rule into a pure transform and constrained it well -- the four named mutations plus a fifth all die (see below) -- but the wiring from the only production consumer to that transform is now unconstrained. tdd-red.sh:31 shells `tdd_scan.py plan`, never `task-for`, so the seam under test is not the path that ships. Task criterion 'tdd_scan.py must scope the Gradle task to the owning module' has no test that fails without it; criterion 'the rule must be a pure transform' does. Closing it is one assertion over plan() using two ids that already exist in the tree (binjava.binstore.VersionTest, binjava.CoverageGateTest), which also pins the buildSrc-vs-module distinction on the shipped path.
findings.failure_scenario: An agent refactoring plan() -- or a partial revert, or a merge resolving toward the old body -- inlines the task computation again and drops the task_for call. task_for survives as a correct, fully tested, dead function; plan() emits the bare root task `test`; `./gradlew test --tests <one class>` fans out across all eight modules at org.gradle.parallel=true; the M1.0 defect returns verbatim (2 of 7 ids recorded) with the harness suite green and TddPlanScopeTest still asserting the transform nobody calls.
